Observable JS is Quarto's native client-side reactive runtime. Unlike Jupyter Widgets it
needs no widget manager: cells re-evaluate in dependency order in the browser. This note
checks that the runtime survives extraction into the Quartz page frame, and that data
computed in Python reaches it. Background in [[Monte Carlo Simulation]].

## Handing data from Python to Observable

`ojs_define` serialises a Python value into the page for the Observable runtime to pick up.

```{python}
#| label: convergence-series
sample_sizes = [10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000]
errors = [0.25, 0.16, 0.09, 0.06, 0.04, 0.025, 0.018]
series = [{"n": n, "error": e} for n, e in zip(sample_sizes, errors)]
ojs_define(series=series)
```

## A reactive input

Moving the slider must recompute the filtered table and the chart below it without a page
reload. This is the core reactivity test: if the runtime failed to initialise, the input
would not render at all.

```{ojs}
//| label: ojs-input
viewof cutoff = Inputs.range([10, 1000], { value: 1000, step: 10, label: "max samples" })
```

```{ojs}
//| label: ojs-derived
filtered = series.filter((row) => row.n <= cutoff)
```

```{ojs}
//| label: ojs-readout
md`Showing **${filtered.length}** of **${series.length}** points, up to n = **${cutoff}**.`
```

## A reactive chart

The mark colour is read from the page's own CSS custom properties rather than named
here, so the chart tracks the shared palette (and stays correct under both page themes)
without a copy of it baked into this document.

```{ojs}
//| label: ojs-palette
//| echo: false
seriesColor = (n) => getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue(`--qmd-chart-series-${n}`).trim()
```

```{ojs}
//| label: ojs-plot
Plot.plot({
  marks: [
    Plot.line(filtered, { x: "n", y: "error", stroke: seriesColor(1) }),
    Plot.dot(filtered, { x: "n", y: "error", fill: seriesColor(1) })
  ],
  x: { type: "log", label: "samples" },
  y: { type: "log", label: "absolute error" },
  height: 300
})
```

## A reactive table

```{ojs}
//| label: ojs-table
Inputs.table(filtered)
```

Compare with the widget approach in [[Jupyter Widgets]].
